name: Los Thuthanaka
label: Self-released
lede: Two Aymara siblings put a 61-minute record on Bandcamp with no warning, and Pitchfork ranked it first among the albums of 2025.

eras.title: From E+E to Elysia Crampton
eras.text: Before the duo existed, Chuquimamani-Condori recorded as E+E and then as Elysia Crampton, stitching Southern hip-hop, Andean folk and long stretches of Virginia and Bolivia into collages.

years.src: Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival · Wikipedia: Chuquimamani-Condori
years.h: E+E starts out as a crowd, not a solo act
years.p: Vice dates the E+E name to 2008: a handle for mixes, edits and a rotating set of collaborators, not one performer.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the E+E name earlier, in the early 2000s, and says the artist began writing and recording in 2007 with Erik Ansaya and Ashland Mines. Vice's 2016 interview gives 2008. Either way, the project was loose: contributing writers, plus DJ mixes made from keyboard, acapellas and a sampler.

Vice also reports that the artist grew up in a small town near Monterrey, Mexico, took piano lessons as a child, and spent time in Virginia and La Paz. The artist described that mobility as key to survival.

years.src: Wikipedia: American Drift · Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival
years.h: American Drift starts in Roanoke and gets finished in La Paz
years.p: Elysia Crampton's first album on Blueberry Recordings began in 2012 in Roanoke and Richmond, Virginia. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the record draws on crunk and Southern hip-hop, Bolivian and Peruvian prog rock, black spirituals, blues, huayno and cumbia, and ties precolonial Aymara history to African-American history. Pitchfork said it "represents a monumental undertaking."

Vice reports that the artist's grandfather died in late fall 2015 while the record was in its final stretch, and that the family's Italian restaurant in Weyers Cave, Virginia is part of the backstory. Parts of the record were finished in La Paz.

years.cap: Elysia Crampton performing at OBEY Convention X.
years.src: Wikipedia: Elysia Crampton Presents: Demon City · Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival
years.h: Billed as an epic poem, Demon City lines up [[Rabit|2e6c4963-cb32-4276-8b51-9c2c61de19ca]] and [[Chino Amobi|1eaf159e-e986-42d4-b151-79a8c2512682]]
years.p: Released July 22, 2016 on Break World Records, the 25-minute record also credits Why Be and Lexxi.
years.xp:
The second track is titled "After Woman (For Bartolina Sisa)," a nod to the 18th-century Aymara resistance leader. Wikipedia lists a Metacritic aggregate of 88 and a Pitchfork score of 8.2, and quotes Pitchfork calling it "a wonder of concision."

Vice reports that the artist's grandmother Flora is one of the record's dedicatees.

eras.title: A new name, unmastered
eras.text: Chuquimamani-Condori takes an Aymara name, finishes a commission for a Geneva show and keeps self-releasing, and the sound gets louder, dirtier and easier to dance to. Brother Joshua Chuquimia Crampton starts putting out hours of solo guitar.

years.p: Wikipedia lists the July 25, 2019 self-release as the first under the Aymara name given by the artist's mother, replacing Elysia Crampton.

years.h: A Geneva commission becomes ORCORARA 2010, with proceeds to AIM SoCal
years.p: Made for a 2018 Geneva show, released digitally May 1, 2020 on PAN and on vinyl July 10, mastered by Rashad Becker.
years.xp: XLR8R reports the piece honors Paul Sousa, an incarcerated man who served as a firefighter in California's Sierra Nevada. Proceeds went to American Indian Movement West and AIM SoCal.

years.h: Joshua Chuquimia Crampton's solo debut runs 96 minutes of guitar
years.p: The Heart's Wash is 15 pieces of solo guitar, written in non-traditional notation, per Wikipedia. 4 (2021) and Profundo Amor (2023) followed.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Crampton was born in 1983 in San Diego and raised partly in rural Mexico, and credits his grandparents with teaching him Andean rhythms. He names two childhood concerts as formative: Los Kjarkas and the Smashing Pumpkins.

years.h: DJ E arrives with no label and ends up No. 9 on Pitchfork's 2020s list
years.p: The 29-minute self-release got 8.0 from Pitchfork, which later placed it ninth among the best albums of the 2020s so far.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes it as a densely layered collage of siku panpipes, synths, grand piano and a circular saw, deliberately unmastered as a rejection of "clean" sound. Pitchfork's Sam Goldner called it a binary-smashing collage.

Wikipedia calls it the first album released under the Aymara name Chuquimamani-Condori, which is at odds with the 2019 date given for Quirquincho Medicine above.

eras.title: Two siblings, one name
eras.text: In March 2025 the two put out one record under one name, and Pitchfork, Paste and The Wire all place it in their top three of the year.

years.src: Stereogum: Stream Chuquimamani-Condori · Wikipedia: Los Thuthanaka
years.h: Los Thuthanaka appears on Bandcamp with no warning
years.p: Eight instrumentals, 60:42 in all, credited to Chuquimamani-Condori and Joshua. Nothing announced it first.
years.xp:
Stereogum's Chris DeVille wrote that the record is pounding, throbbing, wonderfully tactile music, and compared its club-plus-live-band setup to Darkside. The artist's statement, quoted by Stereogum, calls the record a milestone with prayers for rain and gratitude.

Wikipedia lists Chuquimamani-Condori on keyboards, sampler, CDJ, ronroco and bombo, and Joshua on guitar, bass and artwork. It says the record is dedicated to Chuqi Chinchay, a figure tied to queer guardianship in Aymara belief.

years.h: Andean dance forms, run through CDJs and left clipped
years.p: Five of the eight tracks run past eight minutes, built like continuous DJ mixes, with static and clipping left in on purpose.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the record rebuilds huayño, caporal and kullawada through ronroco, bombo italaque drums, keytar, electric guitars and CDJs. Track titles carry Aymara translations. The longest, "Kullawada 'Awila'," runs 11:32; the shortest, "Caporal 'Apnaqkaya Titi'," 3:04.

years.big: "Ceremonial but swaggy, cataclysmic but healing, unrefined but magnificent."
q: An easy shortlist contender for 2025's best album.
years.src: Wikipedia: Los Thuthanaka · Album of the Year · Stereogum: Stream Chuquimamani-Condori
years.h: Pitchfork scores it 9.3, then ranks it No. 1 of 2025
years.p: Joshua Minsoo Kim's verdict in Pitchfork. Per Wikipedia, 9.3 is the site's highest score since Fiona Apple's Fetch the Bolt Cutters (2020).
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's rating as 93 out of 100 for a March 22, 2025 release date. Wikipedia's reception section also lists Paste at No. 2, The Wire at No. 3 and Stereogum at No. 14 on their year-end lists.

DeVille wrote his line after one listen, in a Stereogum post dated March 26, 2025.

years.h: Fan cameras follow the tour from Cafe OTO to Brussels
years.p: Fan-shot sets survive from Cafe OTO in London, the Empty Bottle in Chicago and Botanique in Brussels.

years.cap: Chuquimamani-Condori at the Venice Biennale Musica, October 2025.
years.h: Venice gives Chuquimamani-Condori a Silver Lion
years.p: Wikipedia reports the Silver Lion went to Chuquimamani-Condori in 2025, and the Biennale programmed a Los Thuthanaka set.
years.xp: The Biennale Musica programme listed both a Los Thuthanaka performance and a separate solo piece, Cry of Our Guardian Star. The Biennale's own award page could not be fetched, so the wording of the citation is not given here.

eras.title: Anata, then Wak'a
eras.text: Joshua's solo record Anata lands in February. The duo's Wak'a EP follows in April, built on years of gathering Aymara oral histories.

years.h: Joshua turns the gain up on Anata, 25 minutes in the red
years.p: Self-released February 4, 2026. Pitchfork gave it 7.6, with Daniel Bromfield calling it some of the most elemental in-the-red music ever recorded.

yt: Full set, El Rey Theatre, Los Angeles, June 16, 2026
years.h: A 14-page booklet, The Lake Before the Sun Was Born, ships with Wak'a
years.p: Released April 3, 2026: three tracks, 18:27. Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the duo spent years gathering Aymara oral histories from community members and archives for the text. Pitchfork's Sasha Geffen said it commemorates their work to preserve Aymara lore.
